briefings.title: Fed’s Christopher Waller Talks Higher Yields, Inflation | Bloomberg Talks
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller noted that a surge in long-term US Treasury yields is helping cool interest-rate-sensitive sectors like housing and autos, functioning as a de facto rate hike.

briefings.title: FOMC Press Conference, September 16, 2026
briefings.tldr: The FOMC raised the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 3.75% to 4%, citing persistent inflation above its 2% goal, resilient economic growth, and strong labor markets.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Warsh Holds News Conference on Interest Rates
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh announced that the FOMC voted unanimously to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by a quarter percentage point to 3.25%–4%, citing persistent above-target inflation and broader-than-expected economic strength.

briefings.title: LIVE: Fed chair Kevin Warsh speaks as Federal Reserve raises key interest rate
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by a quarter-point to 3.75–4% to combat persistently high inflation, marking the first rate increase since 2023.

briefings.title: Treasury Sec. Bessent and Larry Kudlow participate in a fireside chat at G20 meeting — 9/1/26
briefings.tldr: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and host Larry Kudlow attribute a booming U.S. economy to President Trump's tax cuts, deregulation, and energy expansion, while detailing aggressive economic warfare and blockades to asphyxiate the Iranian regime.

briefings.title: IMF Chief Praises Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole Speech
briefings.tldr: IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech for its clarity on price stability, while warning that high global debt levels and rapid technological innovation complicate central bank efforts to manage inflation.

briefings.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh at Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh used his Jackson Hole address to outline a framework for monetary policy centered on humility, reduced forward guidance, and vigilance against persistent inflation.

briefings.title: Warsh Says Inflation Isn’t Slowing, Vows to Reach 2% Target (FULL)
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh warned that inflation is not meaningfully slowing and remains above the 2% target, emphasizing that the central bank must be confident in underlying inflation trends before easing policy further.

briefings.title: The Kansas City Fed President on the First Jackson Hole of the Warsh Era | Odd Lots

people.name: Jeffrey Schmid
people.role: President and CEO, Kansas City Fed

briefings.tldr: Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid discusses the 49th Jackson Hole symposium, focusing on financial innovation in payments, demographic labor shifts, and navigating above-target inflation under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh.

briefings.title: FOMC Press Conference, July 29, 2026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve voted 9-to-3 to maintain the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75%, emphasizing a new chapter of unfiltered market observation and vigorous internal debate to decisively bring inflation down to its strict 2% target.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks after Fed holds interest rates steady — 7/29/2026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve voted 9-3 to hold the federal funds rate steady at 3.5% to 3.75%, amid strong economic resilience and elevated inflation, while three dissenting officials advocated for an immediate rate hike.

briefings.title: Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh testifies before Senate Banking Committee
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh testified before the Senate Banking Committee for his first semiannual monetary policy report, defending the Fed's independence and emphasizing an ongoing capital investment and AI-driven productivity boom while facing sharp questioning over past financial disclosures, institutional culture, and the central bank's dual mandate amid persistent inflation.

briefings.title: Fireside chat with Governor Barr on artificial intelligence and financial inclusion, July 14, 2026
briefings.tldr: While generative AI offers transformative potential to bridge economic gaps through increased worker productivity and personalized financial tools, Governor Michael Barr emphasizes that these benefits will only materialize through intentional design, robust regulatory guardrails, and a focus on building consumer trust.

briefings.title: Governor Cook moderates the “Emerging Innovation, AI and Financial Inclusion” panel, July 14, 2026
briefings.tldr: AI is democratizing high-quality financial advice and expanding credit access for underserved communities by leveraging alternative data and behavioral science, provided that developers prioritize rigorous, iterative "evals" and augment rather than replace human judgment.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh Testifies on Economy
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh testified before the House Financial Services Committee, emphasizing his absolute commitment to restoring price stability, protecting central bank independence, and reforming the Fed through five newly established task forces addressing communications, balance sheets, data, AI/productivity, and inflation frameworks.

briefings.title: LIVE: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh Delivers Key Speech at ECB Central Banking Forum
briefings.tldr: At the European Central Bank (ECB) Forum on Central Banking in Sintra, global central bank leaders strongly reaffirmed their commitment to institutional independence while discussing the transition from lagging economic indicators to real-time data analytics.

briefings.title: CNBC's Sara Eisen moderates a policy panel at the ECB Forum on Central Banking 2026 — 7/1/26
briefings.tldr: At the 2026 ECB Forum, central bank leaders from the ECB, Federal Reserve, Bank of England, and Bank of Canada signaled a coordinated shift away from rigid forward guidance toward "framework guidance," highlighting divergent regional economic pressures and the massive, hard-to-measure impacts of AI on productivity and financial stability.

briefings.title: The Q2 2026 Report Card: Who Won, Who Lost, and Why | The Weekly Wrap
briefings.tldr: While Q2 2026 saw strong overall gains for the S&P 500 (+13%) and Nasdaq (+18%), a critical market shift occurred as investors fled capital-intensive tech "hyperscalers" lacking competitive moats in favor of scarce hardware plays like Micron, while software and consulting sectors suffered severe AI-driven disruption.

briefings.title: Inside Economics #280 - Breaking in a New Chair
briefings.tldr: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) unanimously voted 12–0 to keep interest rates steady at 3.5% to 3.75% during Kevin Warsh's first meeting as Fed Chair, but the panel expressed strong concerns over Warsh's shift toward a highly minimalist, less transparent communication style and his proposed structural reforms.

briefings.title: Watch CNBC's full interview with White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett

people.name: Kevin Hassett
people.role: Director, White House National Economic Council

briefings.tldr: NEC Director Kevin Hassett details the White House’s strategy to lower the national debt through federal workforce cuts and pro-growth tax policies, while highlighting a highly profitable AI boom and successful diplomatic efforts easing global oil markets.

briefings.title: Welcoming remarks by Governor Waller, June 22, 2026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve’s Fifth Conference on the International Roles of the U.S. Dollar focuses on how digital innovations, particularly stablecoins and distributed ledger technology, are reshaping global financial intermediation and the dollar's traditional dominance.

briefings.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks after Federal Reserve leaves interest rates unchanged | full video
briefings.tldr: At his first meeting as Federal Reserve Chairman, Kevin Warsh announced the FOMC's decision to maintain interest rates at 3.5% to 3.75% while launching five strategic task forces to reform Fed operations.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh News Conference
briefings.tldr: In his first press conference as Federal Reserve Chair, Kevin Warsh announced the FOMC’s decision to hold interest rates at 3.5% to 3.75% while introducing five sweeping task forces to modernize the central bank’s communication, balance sheet, data analytics, inflation framework, and approach to productivity.

briefings.title: President Trump swears in Kevin Warsh as the new Federal Reserve chair — 5/22/2026
briefings.tldr: President Donald J. Trump swore in Kevin Warsh as the new Federal Reserve Chair, urging him to maintain absolute independence and steer the central bank back to its core mission of price stability and full employment.

briefings.title: Powell Is Out, Warsh Is In: What It Means for Crypto
briefings.tldr: As Kevin Warsh prepares to succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve Chair, global bond yields signal severe macro tightening while stock markets reach all-time highs on AI hype.

people.name: Julia La Roche
people.role: Host, The Julia La Roche Show

briefings.tldr: Chris Whalen warns that double-digit inflation is possible by year-end due to energy shortages and Middle East conflict, while the Federal Reserve prepares for a tectonic shift under Kevin Warsh toward a supply-side, market-driven policy regime.

briefings.title: 🔴 DIRECTO VISIÓN GLOBAL | Trump abandona China sin grandes acuerdos y Warsh se estrena en la FED
briefings.tldr: Donald Trump’s historic visit to Beijing concluded with modest commercial gains (Boeing, Nvidia) and a fragile diplomatic truce, while Kevin Warsh succeeds Jerome Powell as Fed Chair amid stagflationary pressures and low consumer confidence.

briefings.title: Boston Fed President Collins on FOMC Dissent and Kevin Warsh’s Nomination | Big Take
briefings.tldr: Boston Fed President Susan Collins supports the recent shift toward policy dissent, arguing against an "easing bias" as the war in Iran and persistent supply shocks delay inflation's return to the 2% target.

briefings.title: Jerome Powell is Fueled by Pure Righteous Anger—And We LOVE IT (w/ Andrew Weissmann) | Illegal News
briefings.tldr: Former DOJ official Andrew Weissmann and Sarah Longwell analyze the Supreme Court’s rapid intervention in Louisiana redistricting and the surge of "retributive" investigations targeting the Federal Reserve, election workers, and political adversaries.

briefings.title: Jerome Powell Decides to Stay on the Federal Reserve Board of Governors
briefings.tldr: Kevin Warsh is set to become Federal Reserve Chairman amid an AI-driven but inflationary economy, while outgoing Chair Jerome Powell’s unprecedented decision to remain on the Board of Governors creates a complex leadership dynamic that limits the Trump administration’s ability to appoint a new majority.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell speaks after Fed holds interest rates steady — 4/29/26
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.5%–3.75% amid "misbehaving" inflation and geopolitical uncertainty, while Chair Jerome Powell announced he will remain on the Board as a Governor after his chairmanship ends to protect the institution from unprecedented political and legal attacks.

briefings.title: Weekly Washington Policy Pulse: War Powers, Iran Defense, Warsh Nod (April 13, 2026) | Balance...
briefings.tldr: Congress enters a high-velocity legislative window ahead of the 2026 midterms, prioritizing a two-part reconciliation strategy to fund the Department of Homeland Security and a massive $80–$200 billion defense supplemental targeting Iranian threats.

briefings.title: LIVE: Federal Reserve Chief Jerome Powell Speaks at Harvard University
briefings.tldr: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell reaffirms the Fed’s commitment to a 2% inflation target despite emerging supply shocks from tariffs and energy prices, while emphasizing that institutional independence and bipartisan stewardship are critical to maintaining economic stability.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell speaks at Harvard University — 3/30/2026
briefings.tldr: Fed Chair Jerome Powell reaffirmed the FOMC’s commitment to a 2% inflation target despite new pressures from tariffs and energy shocks, while emphasizing that the U.S. financial system is significantly more resilient than it was prior to the 2008 crisis.

briefings.title: LIVE: Fed Chair Jerome Powell delivers remarks at Harvard University
briefings.tldr: Fed Chair Jerome Powell reaffirmed the Federal Reserve's unwavering commitment to a 2% inflation target while highlighting the U.S. economy's remarkable resilience and productivity.

briefings.title: Wall Street Week | Fed on Iran War, AI Expectations
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve is maintaining a "higher for longer" interest rate stance due to geopolitical uncertainty and domestic fiscal stimulus, while experts suggest the AI revolution may be a gradual integration of "normal technology" rather than an immediate economic upheaval.

briefings.title: Powell discusses Fed's decision to keep rates unchanged amid pressure from Trump | full video
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve is maintaining current interest rates as it navigates a "difficult balance" between persistent inflation—driven by tariffs and energy shocks—and emerging downside risks in the labor market.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell speaks after Fed holds interest rate steady — 3/18/2026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve held interest rates steady at 3.5%–3.75% as it navigates a "difficult situation" characterized by upside risks to inflation from Middle East oil shocks and tariffs, contrasted against downside risks in a cooling labor market.

briefings.title: JUST IN: Jerome Powell Holds Briefing After Fed Holds Interest Rates, Warns Of Iran War Uncertainty
briefings.tldr: The Federal Reserve elected to maintain interest rates at 3.5%–3.75%, balancing a resilient economy and stable labor market against "frustratingly" persistent inflation and new economic uncertainties stemming from the Middle East conflict.

briefings.title: WATCH LIVE: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell Briefs Press After Open Markets Committee Meeting
briefings.tldr: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) maintained the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75%, opting for a "wait-and-see" approach as the Fed balances persistent inflation—driven by tariffs and Middle East energy shocks—against a softening labor market that shows signs of zero net job creation in the private sector.

briefings.title: BREAKING NEWS: Jeanine Pirro Holds Briefing After Judge Blocks Subpoenas In Jerome Powell Case
briefings.tldr: U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced the DOJ will appeal an "activist" ruling by Judge James Boasberg that blocked grand jury subpoenas investigating Federal Reserve Chairman Jerome Powell for $1 billion in renovation cost overruns.

briefings.title: Understanding Kevin Warsh's Plan for the Fed | Trumponomics
briefings.tldr: Kevin Warsh is expected to transition from a historical "inflation hawk" to a pragmatic, productivity-focused Fed Chair who prioritizes market signals and private-sector data over traditional economic models while seeking closer "soft coordination" with the Treasury on balance sheet management.

briefings.title: How a Former Fed Vice-Chair Is thinking About the Next Fed Chair | Odd Lots
briefings.tldr: Former Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida views Kevin Warsh as a sensible pick for Fed Chair who will prioritize supply-side economics and a collaborative relationship with the Treasury.

briefings.title: Warsh Call for New Fed-Treasury Accord Unsettles Bond Market
briefings.tldr: Former Fed Vice Chair Richard Clarida suggests that a potential "Kevin Warsh Fed" would likely pivot toward a new Fed-Treasury accord focused on balance sheet composition rather than yield caps, while potentially guiding interest rates down to 3%.

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell speaks as Fed holds key interest rate steady  1282026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Open Market Committee maintained its policy rate at 3.5%-3.75%, concluding that prior rate cuts have appropriately positioned monetary policy to pursue its dual mandate.
